gateway.text:
### DNA repair, simply

```text
DNA = a set of instructions

     DNA gets damaged
          ↓
   🚨 Cell notices
          ↓
   ⏸️ Cell pauses
          ↓
   🛠️ Repair team fixes it
          ↓
   ▶️ Cell keeps working
```

Different repair teams fix different problems:

- **Small mistake:** replace one DNA “letter.”
- **Big damaged spot:** cut it out and replace it.
- **Broken DNA:** join the pieces back together.
- **Hard-to-fix damage:** the cell may stop dividing or die.

DNA repair is really a group of processes—not one single repair system [DNA repair basics](/education/concepts/cancer-biology/genome-instability-and-repair/dna-damage-and-repair-overview/#how-it-works). A **checkpoint** is simply the cell’s pause button. It gives the repair team time to work, but pausing does not guarantee that the damage was fixed.

Would you like an even simpler cartoon about **BRCA**, one of the DNA-repair helpers?
